name: Adnah
overview: Adnah was a male military leader noted in Scripture as a commander of 300,000 men under King Jehoshaphat. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his role as a commander highlights his significant leadership position during Jehoshaphat's reign. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Adnah means 'delight' in the original language. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but serves as a meaningful identifier for this individual. No further titles are associated with him in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Adnah beyond his military role under Jehoshaphat. There are no listed relatives or descendants connected to him in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Adnah's significance lies in his leadership as a commander of a large army during the reign of Jehoshaphat, demonstrating the organized military strength of Judah at that time. His mention underscores the importance of military readiness and faithful service within God's people. Though details are sparse, his role contributes to the broader narrative of God's provision and protection over His kingdom through capable leaders.
